title: Prospective comparison of bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) and CT-based body and organ analysis (BOA) for the assessment of body composition and nutritional status in patients prior to major abdominal surgery.
summary:
Many patients undergoing major abdominal surgery have impaired nutritional status or altered body composition before surgery, for example reduced muscle mass. This may influence recovery after surgery and the risk of postoperative complications.
This study compares two methods for assessing body composition and nutritional status: bioelectrical impedance analysis, BIA, and computer-assisted analysis of already available CT images, referred to as CT-based body and organ analysis, BOA.
BIA is a short, non-invasive measurement using a very weak, non-perceptible electrical current to estimate parameters such as body water, fat mass, and muscle mass. No additional CT scan is performed for the study. Instead, CT images that are already available for clinical reasons are analyzed.
The aim of the study is to determine whether the easily applicable BIA measurement provides similar information on body composition and nutritional status as CT-based analysis. In addition, the study will investigate whether these parameters are associated with preoperative nutritional risk, postoperative complications, and length of hospital stay.
Participation involves a one-time BIA measurement during the regular preoperative outpatient visit. In addition, existing routine clinical data from the medical record will be analyzed. No additional CT scans, no additional follow-up visits, and no study-related treatment are performed. The study is a prospective, multicenter, non-interventional observational study.
conditions: Preoperative nutritional status and body composition in patients undergoing major abdominal surgery, particularly preoperative malnutrition, reduced muscle mass/sarcopenia, and unfavorable body composition as perioperative risk factors.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age ≥ 18 years
Scheduled major abdominal surgery, e.g., colorectal, hepatobiliary, pancreatic, gastric, or retroperitoneal surgery
Availability of a preoperative CT scan performed for clinical reasons, usually within ≤ 6 weeks prior to surgery
Feasibility of a standardized bioelectrical impedance analysis, BIA, in standing or supine position depending on the device
Capacity to provide informed consent
Written voluntary informed consent after comprehensive information about the study
Exclusion criteria:
Presence of implantable electronic devices, e.g., pacemaker or implantable cardioverter-defibrillator, ICD, for which BIA is contraindicated
Poor CT image quality or missing slice data preventing CT-based body and organ analysis, BOA
Emergency or acute surgery preventing preoperative study enrollment and BIA measurement
Pregnancy, if listed as a contraindication for BIA by the device manufacturer
Lack of capacity to provide informed consent or refusal to participate in the study
Insufficient language skills preventing complete study information and informed consent
